title: Check Robot Command Database Model Table for Active Command Status (Sent → In Progress → Archived)
summary: Use the Robotics module’s transactional table, RobotCommandDatabaseModel, to determine whether a robot command is still active (sent/in-progress) or has completed and been archived to Robot Command Activity (historical status such as errored or cancelled).
when_to_use: When you need to verify whether a specific Robotics-module robot command for an AGV is still active (sent/in-progress) or has completed and moved into the archived Robot Command Activity record.
roles_and_responsibilities: L2_support: Execute the database checks in RobotCommandDatabaseModel and Robot Command Activity to confirm command lifecycle state and timing fields.
access_or_tools_needed: Access to the Robot Command Database model table (RobotCommandDatabaseModel)
Access to the Robot Command Activity archive view/table

access_required: Robot Command Database model table access (RobotCommandDatabaseModel)
Robot Command Activity archive view/table access
system_preconditions: Robotics module is generating commands that are written into RobotCommandDatabaseModel and later archived to Robot Command Activity when complete.

visual_references.description: Training frame showing RobotCommandDatabaseModel command names and fields (including sent/in-progress indicators and command lifecycle context).

steps.title: Open the Robot Command Database model table view (RobotCommandDatabaseModel)
steps.purpose: Access the active transactional table that tracks Robotics-module robot command lifecycle.
steps.instruction: Open the Robot Command Database model table view for RobotCommandDatabaseModel and display the columns/fields used to identify command lifecycle (including sent time and in-progress time) and command identity fields (command name, robot name, container, station/parameters).
steps.expected_result: RobotCommandDatabaseModel is visible with rows that include command identity fields and lifecycle timing fields (sent time and in-progress time).
steps.healthy_condition: The table shows active command records (the source describes it as a constantly updating transactional table that keeps active commands).
steps.failure_condition: You cannot view RobotCommandDatabaseModel fields needed to identify command lifecycle (sent time / in-progress time) or command identity (command name and associated robot/container/station parameters).

actions.label: Open RobotCommandDatabaseModel table view
actions.exact_action: Open the Robot Command Database model table view (RobotCommandDatabaseModel)

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Robot Command Database model table tracks status of robot commands requested by the Robotics module for AGVs; it is a constantly updating transactional table for active commands only; it shows sent time and in progress time.

steps.title: Locate the relevant active command row by command name and associated parameters
steps.purpose: Find the exact command record in RobotCommandDatabaseModel that corresponds to the Robotics request you are investigating.
steps.instruction: In RobotCommandDatabaseModel, locate the row matching the command name (examples from the source include MoveTote, PickupTote, DropOffTote, EmptyGoTo, RemoveAgv, ReleaseAgv, GoCharge) and match the associated robot name/container/station parameters shown in the table.
steps.expected_result: A single RobotCommandDatabaseModel row is identified for the target command name and the associated robot/container/station parameters.
steps.healthy_condition: The identified row represents an active command record that is currently in the active RobotCommandDatabaseModel table (the source describes active commands are kept here until completion).
steps.failure_condition: No row matches the command name and associated robot/container/station parameters in RobotCommandDatabaseModel.

actions.label: Match command row by identity fields
actions.exact_action: Locate the relevant active command row by matching the command name and the associated robot name/container/station parameters

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: RobotCommandDatabaseModel includes command name, robot name, container and station/parameters sent to the Geek Plus COM module; it tracks status of robot commands requested by Robotics module for AGVs.

steps.title: Check lifecycle timestamps/fields (sent time and in-progress time)
steps.purpose: Determine whether the command is still in the active lifecycle stage (sent vs in-progress).
steps.instruction: For the identified RobotCommandDatabaseModel row, confirm the row has a sent time and determine whether it is marked as in progress by checking the in-progress time field/indicator described in the source.
steps.expected_result: You can classify the command lifecycle state based on the presence/values of sent time and in-progress time (sent but not in-progress vs marked in-progress).
steps.healthy_condition: The row shows sent time, and when it is marked in-progress the source describes that the AGV is marked and the destination queue/location capacity is freed accordingly.
steps.failure_condition: The row does not show sent time, or it appears stuck in a state where it does not progress from sent to in-progress as described by the source.

actions.label: Verify sent and in-progress timing fields
actions.exact_action: Confirm the row has a sent time and determine whether it is marked as in progress (sent time vs in-progress time)

stop_or_escalate_if: If the command appears stuck (e.g., not progressing from sent to in-progress as described), stop and escalate for deeper investigation.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The table shows sent time and in progress time; when we write it to the table we put sent time, and when we get an in progress we mark that AGV; until then there is still a current destination location.

steps.title: If not in active table, confirm archive in Robot Command Activity and review archived status
steps.purpose: Determine whether the command has completed and moved out of the active table into the historical archive, including resolved/failed outcomes.
steps.instruction: If the command is no longer present in RobotCommandDatabaseModel, open the Robot Command Activity archive view/table and search for the historical record for the same command name and associated robot/container/station parameters. Review the archived status, noting that the source states it could be errored or cancelled.
steps.expected_result: A matching historical record is found in Robot Command Activity with an archived status (e.g., errored or cancelled) for the target command.
steps.healthy_condition: The command is absent from RobotCommandDatabaseModel and present in Robot Command Activity as a completed/archived record.
steps.failure_condition: The expected command is not present in RobotCommandDatabaseModel and also not found in Robot Command Activity.

actions.label: Search Robot Command Activity archive
actions.exact_action: Confirm it has been archived to Robot Command Activity and review the archived status (errored/cancelled)

stop_or_escalate_if: If the expected command is not present in RobotCommandDatabaseModel and also not found in Robot Command Activity, stop and escalate for deeper investigation.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: When commands are complete, they're archived to robot command activity; historical status includes outcomes such as errored or cancelled.

steps.title: Interpret queue/capacity implication of in-progress vs not-yet in-progress
steps.purpose: Use the source’s described operational meaning of the lifecycle transition to understand why a destination may appear occupied or freed.
steps.instruction: Using the source’s described relationship between command lifecycle and queue/location capacity, interpret the observed lifecycle state: when the command is in-progress, it frees up the queue/location capacity; until then, the current destination location remains.
steps.expected_result: Your lifecycle classification (sent vs in-progress vs archived) aligns with the expected queue/location capacity behavior described by the source.
steps.healthy_condition: If the command is marked in-progress, the source’s described implication is that the queue/location capacity is freed; if not yet in-progress, the current destination location remains.
steps.failure_condition: The observed lifecycle state does not align with the expected queue/location capacity behavior described by the source (indicating a deeper issue beyond this database-only check).

actions.label: Interpret lifecycle vs queue capacity behavior
actions.exact_action: Interpret the queue/capacity implication described by the source for sent vs in-progress

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Until we get it in progress, you still have a current destination location; when in progress, it frees up that queue/location capacity (source ties this to Robot Location model Max Agvs and tipper capacity).
Robot location model includes Max Agvs; each tipper can only have one (some have two), and in-progress indicates the queue/location is freed.

success_criteria: For the target command, you determine whether it is still active in RobotCommandDatabaseModel (sent and/or in-progress) or has been archived to Robot Command Activity with an archived status (e.g., errored or cancelled).
You can explain the observed lifecycle state using the source’s sent → in-progress → archived model and the described queue/location capacity implication.
healthy_conditions: RobotCommandDatabaseModel contains active command rows with sent time and in-progress time fields.
Completed commands are absent from RobotCommandDatabaseModel and present in Robot Command Activity with a status such as errored or cancelled.
failure_conditions: Target command is missing from RobotCommandDatabaseModel and also missing from Robot Command Activity.
Target command appears stuck (not progressing from sent to in-progress as described).
Lifecycle state cannot be classified due to missing/unclear sent time or in-progress time fields.
escalation_guidance: If the expected command is not present in RobotCommandDatabaseModel and also not found in Robot Command Activity, stop and escalate for deeper investigation (the source does not provide further database-only troubleshooting steps in this segment).

If the command appears stuck (e.g., not progressing from sent to in-progress as described), stop and escalate; the source mentions operational recovery ideas elsewhere but does not provide a specific database-only recovery procedure in this segment.
